🖥 Iran says global refugee support ‘insufficient’ as it hosts millions under sanctions

📌 Tehran, IRNA - Iran’s refugee affairs chief criticized international support for hosting refugees as insufficient, stressing that the country has continued providing public services to millions of refugees and migrants despite sanctions and attacks.

Speaking at the 77th annual session of the Executive Committee of the UN High Commissioner for Refugees (ExCom) in Geneva, Nader Yar-Ahmadi, head of Iran’s Bureau for Aliens and Foreign Immigrants Affairs, stressed that over decades of hosting, Iran has consistently prioritized the rights and human dignity of refugees and foreign migrants.
​
Referring to Afghan nationals’ access to Iran’s education and healthcare services, he said that 59,658 Afghan students are currently studying at Iranian universities and scientific centers, and a significant number of Afghan nationals have also graduated from Iran’s higher education institutions.
​
Yar-Ahmadi stressed that the international community must fulfill its shared responsibility to adequately support host countries.
​
He called for a fair distribution of the responsibility for hosting refugees, increased financial support from the international community, proportionate allocation of resources, and the removal of obstacles preventing host countries from accessing development aid.
​
“In recent years, the financial needs of the UNHCR operation in Iran were estimated at around $140 million, but less than one-tenth of that amount was realized in 2025,” he added.
​
Meanwhile, Barham Salih, the UN High Commissioner for Refugees, expressed gratitude to Iran for its generous and non-discriminatory hosting of refugees over past decades.

🔐 Compliance Data Leak Exposes 291 Crypto Users' Identities

A data leak has linked the real identities of 291 crypto users directly to their wallet activity, stripping away the anonymity they relied on.

Copied support records exposed varying combinations of personal identity, location, and compliance data. Private keys and customer funds were not compromised in the incident.

The breach highlights a persistent vulnerability in crypto: while blockchain transactions can be pseudonymous, KYC and compliance records held by centralized services create a paper trail that, if exposed, can permanently de-anonymize users.

🎙 Gharibabadi heads to Baku for CICA summit

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Deputy Foreign Minister for Legal and International Affairs, Kazem Gharibabadi, has departed for Baku to attend the Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) summit.

Gharibabadi left Tehran for Baku on Wednesday to attend the CICA Summit.
​
At the summit, which brings together the leaders of Asian countries, Gharibabadi will outline Iran’s positions, particularly regarding sources of insecurity in the region and the US and Israeli regimes’ military aggression and crimes against the Iranian people.
​
The CICA was proposed in 1992 at the initiative of then-Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev. Iran is one of the organization’s 28 member states.
​
The seventh CICA Summit is scheduled to open in Baku, the capital of Azerbaijan, on October 15, 2026.
